introduction: OverviewCassius IntroductionCassius is a 4✦ character from the Controller class and Instinct attribute, part of the Peltion [Company 110] faction.Supports his team with consistent card draw and buffs in the form of his unique “Quest” mechanic and Morale generation via neutral epiphanies.

panels.html:
Cassius Review

Pros

  • High additive buffing.

  • One of the best users of 4p Glory Reign, as Cassius is able to generate [Exhaust] Quests to activate its full effect quickly.

  • Extremely high sustain in many gamemodes (Tower, Great-Rift, FSO, etc.) because of the strength of Morale reduction and Fortitude generation.

  • Generates strong draw.

  • Inexpensive to build via Sortie Editing (Common Epiphanies cheaper to reroll).

Cons

  • Pop-Eyed Piper forces the player to choose between either [Initiation] OR ‘Choose Quest’, when both are the most important features–this creates a problem where Cassius’ Turn-1 can be extremely inconsistent without abusing rewinds/restarts.

Introduction for Cassius isn't available yet. It will be added soon.

Review

Key Mechanics

  • Quests: Cassius’ Pop Eyed Popper upgrade randomly starts one of four Quests, which last until the end of battle. These Quests can be completed just by playing cards and they grant free Quest Cards with decent effects.

    • Triple 0: Play 3 cards that cost 0 AP.

      • Deals a base 200% damage, +40% per Attack Card used this turn, up to a maximum of 4.

    • Triple 1: Play 3 cards that cost 1 AP.

      • Deals 150% damage, heals for 150% and also draws 1 card.

    • Straight: Play 3 cards that cost 0, 1 and 2 AP each.

      • For 1 turn(s), gain 2 stacks of Morale, Resolve and Fortitude and draw 1 card.

    • Full House: Play 1 card from each Combatant.

      • Draw 1 card and will decrease the stress of 1 random ally by 2.

  • Full House is the best option here—if you’re lucky enough to get it, mainly because its activation condition is extremely easy to fulfill and getting a free Draw 1 so easily is great.

  • Triple 1 technically has a stronger quest reward than Full House, offering damage, a heal and a draw, but unfortunately, it’s far harder to complete, making it a much more niche quest to aim for. 

  • Triple 0 is very difficult for Cassius to complete on his own, as all of his cards cost ≥1 AP at base; Dice Trick can be discounted to 0…but only if you complete 2 Quests first, creating a catch-22 situation. If you don’t have the right teammates, this Quest can brick for the entire fight. The Quest Card works as a nice single-target finisher after spamming a lot of 0-cost attacks.

  • Straight is also a difficult Quest to complete, as playing 2 AP cards isn’t something you can do particularly often unless you have access to AP generation. Because both Morale and Resolve affect card multipliers, you want to complete this Quest at the start of your turn to take full advantage of its effects. Quest progress carries over between turns, so we recommend leaving the 0-cost or 1-cost card until last so you can complete the Quest at the start of a turn.

  • Reduced Morale: Reduced Morale causes enemies to lose a -20% damage multiplier per stack of Reduced Morale they have. This is especially effective at mitigating damage from enemy Consecutive Attacks.

  • Fortitude:  Fortitude provides a -20% damage taken buff per stack of Fortitude you possess. 

  • Resolve: Resolve grants +20% to Shield amounts gained per stack of Resolve.

Review

Preconstructed Decks

Decks not named in this section are generally not recommended to be bought. This does not mean they have no use ever or are not viable, but that our opinion is there are better uses for currency because they are too niche or easy to make with minimal save data editing tools. 

[Dice Trick] - This deck, coincidentally named Dice Trick, focuses on using the Dice Trick card in order to generate 12 Morale a turn (+1 per Quest generated from Pot-7) in order to easily net enough Morale to near the cap. The main draw of this deck is it utilizes an extremely rare Divine (Draw 1 Card of this unit), making it more worth taking than most preconstructed decks because of the expensive nature of editing this normally. Moreover, decks that are purchased are able to be edited, so it’s possible to remove 1 Dice Trick and make slight edits to optimize its use of Faint Memory (Save Data Points), if needed.

Deck utilizes Cassius' ability to move Heidemarie's swords from discard into draw-pile, and Nia's ego skill ability to discard all from draw-pile in order to trigger the discard extra attack of a massive amount of Heidemarie swords all at once. The strategy generally consists of making swords until the turn where you want to nuke and then using Cassius' Shuffle and Nia's Ego. There is a popular variant using more Cassius' Shuffle III's for use against bosses which trigger a lot of stress/mindbreak, since it enables you to Nia Ego Skill multiple times after mindbreak.
Used in
Heidemarie (Sword, Shuffle, Slide!), Nia (Discard DPS Support)
Synergies

Cassius Synergies

Sereniel
  • Cassius can help her break the boss’s Tenacity Bar more efficiently than most allies since he plays Instinct Attack cards and Sereniel boosts Instinct Tenacity damage.
  • He can give her a really high amount of additive buffs that she scales with and if you have AP Sereniel (Divine AP on Homing Laser), she makes the requirements for his build way lower than alternative options.
  • Because Sereniel herself generally has a very low draw requirement in an optimized build, his low but decent net draw is typically well-suited for her needs to a tee.
Hugo
  • He can create up to 4 skill cards per turn very consistently, which allows Hugo’s Commence the Hunt uptime to be easier.
  • Most of his cards double as attacks for proc’ing Hugo Commence the Hunt.
  • His buffs are extremely high value on Extra Attackers, like Hugo, since additive buffs are multiplied by the Extra damage% mechanic.
Selena
  • Joker has the ability to target her order-dependent cards to get more value out of them.
  • They both have high synergy with Sereniel, Heidemarie, and other shared units making them even more synergistic wholistically.
  • Much like Hugo, Extra Attacks benefit from additive buffs even more than most other units, especially ones who do as many Extra Attacks as she or Hugo can.
Heidemarie
  • Cassius is able to easily utilize Triple-1 in Heidemarie's builds that use Sword Rain III, as it will count as playing 5 1-costs in quick succession.
  • Extra Attacks benefit more from buffs than other damage types, and Heidemarie is also is a multi-hitter who benefits from additive buffers like Cassius specifically well.
  • One of Cassius' occasional drawbacks with some units is his buffs not going out before the damage of the ally guaranteed, but Heidemarie's main form of outputting damage often happening from a few cards at the end of turn makes it easier.
Diana
  • Diana is one of the few characters who is able to utilize Cassius' Straight Quest, allowing her to get more Morale buffs from him than alternative options. This is because her 2-cost [Quietus] cards count for the Quests.
  • Extra Attacks benefit more from buffs than other damage types, and Diana is also is a multi-hitter who benefits from additive buffers like Cassius specifically well.
  • Cassius has a variety of ways to Discard, which synergizes with Diana's need for Discard to activate certain effects.

When playing Cassius as a support, if possible, we recommend building him toward having 701+ HP in the character screen so that his Potential 7 is fully active and grants Fortitude every time a Quest is activated. This isn't a mandatory stat goal, but in certain Cassius builds and encounters is an incredibly potent defensive tool.
Investment

Cassius Potential Priority

  • 3-1: Grants a 30% chance to Draw 1 to both of Cassius’ Basic Attacks. 30% isn’t enough to count on, but it can help a little bit early in your run if you draw poorly. It’s not as impactful as some other Combatants’ 3-1s can be.

  • 5-1: Increases his Basic Attacks’ damage. Makes them a little better to play in conjunction with 3-1, but you’ll likely still end up removing them from your deck.

  • 7: Incredible. Getting Morale and Fortitude for a turn every time you complete a Quest makes Cassius an even more potent support. You already want to complete Quests early in a turn, but this makes it even more important if you want to take advantage of Morale.

Seasonal

Cassius Seasonal Powers

Introduces Desire Cards. Desire Cards are cards that primarily exist to give a strong passive buff from meeting certain Desire Thresholds (3/5/7) which can only be done by having multiple ally decks also made in Season-4. 

  • For Desire Threshold, it’s common to run 1 Claim / 1 Survival / 1 Inquiry for use in a variety of builds on supports; however, it's also common to just do 3 ‘X’ to meet effect easier or do 2 'X' / 1 Inquiry (to keep Sample Collection as Card Effect). This is extremely dependent on ally desire cards and individual team building goal.

’X’ refers to a ‘Placeholder for Specific Desire Threshold Goal’, i.e. if you are building your team for 7 Claim then you might do 2 Claim / 1 Inquiry.

Introduces Persona Cards and Engravings. Persona Cards are powerful cards that introduce new playstyles or ways of buffing/debuffing. Engravings are effects that can be applied to both the Persona Cards and Equipment, functioning near identically to Refinements of Season-2 but with new effects.

  • The most common Card Engraving to take is [For each Lux Engraving, +15% Damage Amount to ally Attack Cards for 1 turn] or [Attunement: Decrease Cost by 1 until used].

  • The most common Equipment Engraving to optimize for is the stacking [When Action Count of enemies is increased by allies, +50% Damage Amount to Ally Attack Cards for 1 turn (1 time per turn)] and [When a card of this unit is activated, 30% to increase Action Count of all enemies by 1 (1 time per turn)], but it's possible to use a variety of other options for a specific set-up (like Discard [Quietus] Engravings when playing high [Quietus] builds or Umbra Engravings just to meet the threshold for certain Persona cards).

Introduces Refinements, effects on Equipment that allow one to get additional Equipment effects for no Faint-Cost (post-S2), and God’s Hammer, a powerful effect that gives a random copy of any other Equipment effect on-top of current Equipment but costs 10 Faint Memory and is only gained from the Boss. 

  • At the start of battle, Draw 1 Exhaust card(s) of this unit.

  • At the start of the turn, if an Exhaust card is in Draw Pile, have a 30% chance to Draw 1 Exhaust card(s).

  • If Damage is completely blocked, at the start of the next turn, increase Damage Amount of allies by 10% for 1 turn (1 time per turn).

  • When Drawing an Exhaust card of this unit through an ally ability, activate immediately (1 time per turn).

Because God’s Hammer is completely RNG at the end of the run, we do not have a specific recommendation since the player has very little control over the decision. Supportive options are recommended for supportive units (like Tentacle or Harp effects).

Introduces Forbidden Cards, powerful cards that create new synergies and can only be acquired once per run (can be duped at one event or via save data editing). 

  • Forbidden: Gesture of Freedom. Permanent Cost-Reduction to 1-card, can be manipulated.

  • Forbidden: Eternal Hunger. +Draw, ++AP (Ally Reliant)

  • Forbidden: Portrait of Fury. ++Draw

  • Forbidden: Guidance of Futility. +++Survivability

Pop Eyed Popper I: In content where you can quickly reset, this can be equal to or better than Pop Eyed V, as both of them usually warrant resetting for the feature that the other gives. However, it can be vastly worse than Pop Eyed IV in scenarios where resetting takes a long time, such as when Cassius is used in second-phase content, where resetting requires you to go through the first phase once again.

Pop Eyed Popper II: [Retain] is added as a tag and the quests no longer [Exhaust] themselves, which can be situationally useful when you would like to keep a card for a future turn, but in well-built teams will often be the equivalent of no Upgrade at all.

Pop Eyed Popper III: This Epiphany still contains the RNG elements of the base card, but it has the benefit of upgrading your quest cards to be noticeably stronger. The only reason it isn’t recommended as resetting for its ideal conditions can be extremely time-consuming and not worth it for most players.

Pop Eyed Popper IV: Being able to choose your quest is an incredible QoL improvement and will save you a vast amount of time that you would need to reset for the others. Thus, it is our top recommendation.

Pop Eyed Popper V: Never take this unless you truly love to gamble.

Neutral: The Neutral versions of this do nothing to improve the card itself and the benefits of whatever Neutral Epiphany you get will likely be outweighed by RNG elements you introduce by not taking an Epiphany that offers more consistency or buffs.

Divine: Which Divine Epiphany to go for will depend on what your team needs and which Epiphany you chose, but here are the main ones to look out for if you have spare Save Data: Morale/Resolve.

Devil Dice I: 3-in-4 chance of a Draw as 3 of the Quest Cards have a Draw effect, but why gamble on the odds when you can guarantee it?

Devil Dice II: One of the best Draws in the game *for one-turn*, as [Retrieve 3] counts down by 1 with every use until the card becomes a Base Devil Dice effectively. Amazing for OTK, especially with Cost Reduction, but not especially strong outside of it.

Devil Dice III: This can be an amazing Draw card, as it could scale up to a theoretical 10-draw per card (if there were 10 targets), but it's conditional for multi-target bosses or multiple enemies. Much lower value outside of AOE.

Devil Dice IV: This one is especially great with other forms of Draw or if you need a way to get cards out of hand, since it can help to cycle cards. In well-optimized decks, it’s typically not going to net you much value over other options, but can be great in certain scenarios where bosses create Status Ailments in hand, for example.

Devil Dice V: The go-to Devil Dice with no Divine Epiphanies, as it is base 0-cost. It has access to +1 AP Divine and Divine Vulnerable (AOE), as well, making it an all-around amazing card.

Neutral: Target Neutral Epiphany: Morale 2.
Cassius has access to high-value Neutral Epiphanies alongside his ability to draw off Quests, combined with the card itself. Devil Dice with Neutral Morale +2 Epiphany can enable him to give +11 Morale (+3 from Quests) off of just Quests and Devil Dice alone.

Divine: Which Divine Epiphany to go for will depend on what your team needs and which Epiphany you chose, but here are the main ones to look out for if you have spare Save Data: +1 AP (Devil Dice III), -1 Cost Reduction, Vulnerable 2.

Shuffle I: Because Shuffle’s primary value comes from Turn 1 re-draw, changing it to [Exhaust 2] tends to be situational. It could end up being an effectively dead card you can’t afford to play if you didn’t factor the context for it well.

Shuffle II: This Epiphany is a pure Upgrade off the base version, allowing you to keep certain cards in hand rather than re-drawing the entire hand entirely.

Shuffle III: Incredibly strong draw, you just leave it in hand until all other cards are played and get 5 draws from it and a free deck re-shuffle.

Shuffle IV: Because of its base 0-cost, this can be a great option if AP is tight. Its effect is situationally very beneficial, allowing you to manipulate up to 5 cards at the top of your draw. and it has strong synergy with other effects that allow you to interact with the top of the Draw Pile, like Nia’s G Chord.

Shuffle V: This loses the [Exhaust] tag and can potentially net you a ton of draw, but more often than not, it’ll be equivalent to 3 Discards – unless you are playing with a ton of high-cost cards or some way to guarantee high-cost cards into the top of the Draw Pile.

Neutral: Target Neutral Epiphany: +1 AP.
Neutral Epiphanies on Shuffle have similar or better effects to Divines on it and will not cost you faint, e.g. there is a 1 AP Neutral Epiphany it can get which effectively makes it free to use without needing a Cost Reduction Divine.

Dice Trick III: This starts at base 0-cost, which, with certain Divine Epiphanies like Vulnerable or AP, can allow it to be used more fluidly in Turn 1 when it can be hard to reduce the cost of Dice Trick. The damage is hard-capped, not at any significant bonus over other options, though.

Dice Trick IV: This offers a non-negligible amount of additional healing and is certainly an option for a healing-based build, but it being locked to [Unique] and Quests being hard-capped makes him often not the ideal choice for a healer.

Dice Trick V: This is an amazing option for an additional +1 Draw ¾ of the time after Turn 1, since 3 out of 4 quests have a Draw feature.

Neutral: Target Neutral Epiphany: +1 AP, Draw 1, Morale 3.
Dice Trick has Neutral pool for 2-3 cost cards, but it effectively becomes 0-cost quite fast. This allows you to get effects like +3 Morale/Fortitude, +1 AP, +1 Draw, etc. on a 0-cost card for no Faint cost.

Divine: Which Divine Epiphany to go for will depend on what your team needs and which Epiphany you chose, but here are the main ones to look out for if you have spare Save Data: Vulnerable 2.
